report.summary: No critical correctness bugs found in visible code. Main risk: cross-process file sharing on Windows may cause PermissionError during append/read, as no sharing flags are set. The 'never collapses' guarantee cannot be verified without the snapshot logic (not shown). Closed vocabulary and disk-change refusal are enforced correctly. Error handling skips corrupt lines as documented; no silent success reporting.
risks: Cross-process file sharing violation on Windows: append opens without explicit sharing flags, potentially denying reads from other processes.
The snapshot implementation is not included in the excerpt; claims about fresh snapshots and immutability cannot be verified.
Global default_log cache could be reset while another thread holds a reference; path change may cause confusion but no crash.
Append is not atomic; a partial write on disk full produces a corrupt line, which is silently skipped on next read (per design, but may lose an event).

handoff.suggestion: Review Windows file sharing: specify FILE_SHARE_READ in open() to avoid PermissionError. Ensure the (unseen) snapshot function does not cache or reuse report objects, as claimed.
